title: docs(adr): ADR-0023 OpenAPI→Connector generator + ADR-0024 MCP servers as connectors
body:
## Summary

Two sibling ADRs for populating the connector registry **without hand-writing each integration**, both staying inside the ADR-0022 open/enterprise boundary.

### ADR-0023 — OpenAPI → Connector Generator
Generate a `Connector` from an OpenAPI 3.x document: one operation → one action (`parameters`+`requestBody` → `inputSchema`, 2xx response → `outputSchema`, `securitySchemes` → static auth). Built **on top of** `@objectstack/connector-rest` — no new engine surface. Covers 'the vendor published a REST spec.'

### ADR-0024 — MCP Servers as Connectors
A generic adapter turns **any MCP server** into a `Connector`: `tools/list` → actions, `connector_action` → `tools/call`. MCP tool shape ≈ `ConnectorActionSchema`, so it's an **adapter, not a port**. One adapter unlocks the whole MCP ecosystem; each server is pure config. The same tools double as ADR-0011 AI tools.

### Why not just import activepieces/n8n pieces?
Both ADRs record the finding: those integrations are **engine-bound code** (`run(ctx)` needs a sandboxed `ActionContext`), not a portable spec. They can be used as endpoint *reference material*, but cannot be dropped into our serializable `Connector` + `(input, ctx)` handler model.

## Status
Both **Proposed**; no shipped code changes. Each ends with concrete follow-ups (scaffold package, CLI, worked example). All code references verified against real files (engine registry, `connector_action` node, `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors` discovery route).
